I’m a PhD Candidate at the Department of Political Science at the University of Gothenburg working on women’s representation in Mixed Member Representative (MMR) systems.
I specialize in text-as-data approaches, with a particular focus on parliamentary language use. As part of my research I have created a complete corpus of speech activity in the New Zealand partliament between 1945 and 2025, and currently working on a proper publication of that data, alongside my PhD.
In addition to my PhD I work on various issues tangentially related to the focus of my dissertation, and I am also attached to the TiNDe project at the University of Oslo, measuring democracy in highly democratic countries.
